content:
dana: heads-up — last two nightly builder runs failed with 401s when trying to push artifacts. started ~02:10 UTC, retries show intermittent 401 then success on fresh run. logs below. anyone seen this pattern?

mike: can you paste the exact error lines + what token source the builder uses? SA impersonation or long-lived key?

ops: tagging ops to check proxy cache TTL @ops

eng-tools-bot: automated-diagnostics: job_id=nightly-build-2026-03-17-02:10; runner=gha-self-hosted-3; token_source=CI_IMPERSONATION; last_success=02:05 UTC; failure_count=2

support-bot: If this affects customers, please file support/priority-1 and include repro steps.

dana: stack excerpt: 
```
2026-03-17T02:10:12Z builder[pid=42] INFO fetch-token: requesting impersonation token
2026-03-17T02:10:12Z builder[pid=42] DEBUG http POST https://auth.redwood.example.com/token 200 OK
2026-03-17T02:10:12Z builder[pid=42] DEBUG token: expires_at=1710000000 (ttl=30s)
2026-03-17T02:10:42Z builder[pid=42] WARN push: received 401 from registry
2026-03-17T02:10:42Z builder[pid=42] DEBUG retry: fetching token cached by proxy
2026-03-17T02:10:42Z builder[pid=42] ERROR push failed: unauthorized (401)
2026-03-17T02:10:44Z builder[pid=42] INFO retry2: fetch atempt -> got new token -> push succeeded
```
Exact message: "unauthorized: invalid credentials"

mike: tl;dr token TTL looks very short (30s in snippet). Are we using our proxy that caches tokens? If proxy returned cached token that was already expired by the time registry validated, that could explain 401 on retry. Which proxy is in path?

dana: yes — builds route through ci-auth-proxy (for local runner speed). Config snippet from proxy logs: 
```
[cache]
max_age = 15
stale_if_error = 5
```
so proxy caches tokens for 15s. builder requests token at T=0, token ttl 30s; retry at T=30s may hit a cached entry that the proxy considered valid but registry rejects (clock skew?).

ops: checking cluster node clocks now — NTP OK, skew <200ms. But registry validates remaining TTL > 5s or so. Could be rounding or boundary condition when token's exp equals request time.

mike: possible race: builder fetches token -> proxy caches it with server-side expiry computed from issued_at + ttl; when builder retries after a failed push it asks proxy for a token again, but proxy returns the cached token (which might be expiring within seconds). Registry sees token as expired. Fix approaches: 1) make proxy avoid returning tokens with <X seconds remaining, 2) increase token TTL from impersonation endpoint, 3) change builder to fetch fresh token for each retry.

dana: repro steps I used: 
1) run a quick loop against local proxy to request token and sleep 25s before using it
2) attempt to push to staging registry -> 401 reproducible when token age >= 28s

command I ran: 
```
TOKEN=$(curl -sS -X POST https://ci-auth-proxy.local/token -d '{"sa":"ci-builder"}' | jq -r .access_token)
sleep 25
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://staging-registry.local/v2/myapp/blobs/uploads/
```

mike: nice repro, thanks. can you also capture proxy response headers `x-cache-age` and token `exp` field? we need to see who is rounding.

eng-tools-bot: probe result (from CI runner network): status=200, proxy_x_cache_age=15s, token_exp=1710000050, issued_at=1710000020, client_time=1710000048

ops: that probe shows token_exp 2s after client_time — so indeed edge case. Looks like TTL calculations might be truncated to seconds and cache policy returns tokens with insufficient remaining life.

mike: quick mitigation: bump proxy cache policy to refuse tokens with <10s remaining. config patch suggestion: 
```
[cache]
min_remaining_secs = 10
max_age = 15
```
Will apply to canary proxy nodes.

dana: if we do that, might increase auth load a bit. Can we also increase impersonation token ttl for ci-builder SA to 60s?

ops: yes we can. I'll open IAM change, but need approval. doing minimal: set ttl to 60s for ci-builder impersonation role and patch proxy to min_remaining_secs=8 as hotfix.

support-bot: please document customer impact window and rollback plan here.

mike: longer-term: change builder retry logic: if push fails with 401, request a fresh token before retry instead of reusing cached token. Also add 500–1500ms jitter between token fetch and push to avoid edge sync issues.

dana: created a tiny GH Actions PR to fetch fresh token on retry + jitter: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/432 (draft).

ops: action plan and owners: 
- ops: apply proxy min_remaining_secs canary -> 10m (owner: ops)
- ops: request IAM change to increase TTL for ci-builder -> 60s (owner: ops)
- mike: merge GH Actions PR to fetch fresh token on retry (owner: mike)
- dana: monitor nightly builds for 24h after changes (owner: dana)

dana: thanks all — I'll watch and report back. :thumbsup:

mike: fyi adding a small dashboard alert for 401 rate on push endpoints to detect regressions (will notify #eng-oncall).

eng-tools-bot: follow-up-check in 6h scheduled.

ops: done — canary applied to 2/4 proxy nodes. observing traffic. current 401s for builder jobs dropped to 0 from 2 in last 10m.

support-bot: note added to incident tracker: INC-2026-0317-01 (no customer escalations).

dana: great, closing loop here.
